items.label: section_header
items.text: KEY POINT

items.label: text
items.text: Several oxides of nitrogen are involved, including NO and NO2. They are often given the general formula NOx.

items.label: caption

items.label: text
items.text: Rain is naturally slightly acidic (pH = ~5.6) because of dissolved carbon dioxide. Acid rain is rain with a pH lower than this (pH < 5.6) because of the presence of various pollutants. The pH of acid rain is often about 4.

items.label: text
items.text: Acid rain is formed when water and oxygen in the atmosphere react with sulfur dioxide to produce sulfuric acid (H2SO), or with various oxides of nitrogen, NO, to give nitric acid (HNO₃). SO2 and NOx come mainly from power stations and factories burning fossil fuels, or from motor vehicles.

items.label: text
items.text: Fossil fuels contain a small amount of sulfur. When the fuel is burned, the sulfur reacts with oxygen, producing sulfur dioxide:

items.label: formula
items.text: S ( s ) + O _ { 2 } ( g ) \rightarrow S O _ { 2 } ( g )

items.label: text
items.text: Reactions in the atmosphere with oxygen and water can convert this to sulfuric acid (H2SO4), a strong acid and an important component of acid rain:

items.label: text
items.text: Note: when sulfur dioxide reacts with water, a weaker acid called sulfurous acid (H_2SO₃) is formed:

items.label: formula
items.text: S O _ { 2 } ( g ) + H _ { 2 } O ( 1 ) \rightarrow H _ { 2 } S O _ { 3 } ( a q )

items.label: text
items.text: In petrol engines, sparks are used to ignite the petrol-air mixture to power the car. The temperature reached in the engine is high enough to allow nitrogen and oxygen in the air to combine to produce oxides of nitrogen. For example:

items.label: formula
items.text: N _ { 2 } ( g ) + O _ { 2 } ( g ) \rightarrow 2 N O ( g )

items.label: text
items.text: These nitrogen oxides can be converted to nitric acid (HNO) in the atmosphere and therefore contribute to acid rain.

items.label: text
items.text: Acid rain is a major problem, mainly because of its devastating effect on trees and on life in lakes. Acid rain kills trees and fish in lakes. In some lakes the water is so acidic that it won't support life at all. Limestone buildings and marble statues (both made of calcium carbonate) and some metals such as iron are also attacked by acid rain.

items.label: text
items.text: Reaction between limestone and sulfuric acid:

items.label: formula
items.text: C a C O _ { 3 } ( s ) + H _ { 2 } S O _ { 4 } ( a q ) \rightarrow C a S O _ { 4 } ( s ) + H _ { 2 } O ( l ) + C O _ { 2 } ( g )

items.label: text
items.text: The solution to acid rain involves removing sulfur from fuels (this is usually done for petrol used in cars), 'scrubbing' the gases from power stations and factories to remove SO2 and NOx, and using catalytic converters in cars.

items.label: section_header
items.text: CRACKING

items.label: text
items.text: Although most of the fractions from the fractional distillation of crude oil are useful as fuels, some fractions are more useful and more profitable to sell than others.

items.label: text
items.text: The amounts of each fraction obtained will depend on the proportions of the various hydrocarbons in the original crude oil, not the amounts in which they are needed. The problem is:

items.label: list_item
items.text: there are far too many long-chain hydrocarbons, which are not in such high demand and are not as profitable to sell

items.label: list_item
items.text: there are not enough shorter-chain hydrocarbons that can be used as fuel for cars.
